claim: RDS Extended Support lets you keep running a database on a major engine version after the RDS end of standard support date, for an additional cost.
question: What is Amazon RDS Extended Support?

evidence.quote: RDS Extended Support allows you to continue running a database on a major engine version past the RDS end of standard support date for an additional cost.

claim: RDS Extended Support is available for up to 3 years past the RDS end of standard support date of a major engine version; after that, if you have not upgraded, Amazon RDS upgrades the major engine version automatically.
question: How long can a database stay in RDS Extended Support, and what happens after that?

values.display: automatically upgrade your major engine version

qualifiers.scope: per major engine version, after the RDS end of standard support date

evidence.quote: RDS Extended Support is available for up to 3 years past the RDS end of standard support date for a major engine version.
After this time, if you haven't upgraded your major engine version to a supported version, then Amazon RDS will automatically upgrade your major engine version.

claim: Unless you disabled RDS Extended Support when you created or restored the DB instance or DB cluster, Amazon RDS enrolls it automatically in Extended Support after the RDS end of standard support date.
question: What happens by default to an RDS database whose major version reaches the end of standard support?

values.display: automatically enroll them in RDS Extended Support

qualifiers.scope: per DB instance or DB cluster

evidence.quote: After the RDS end of standard support date, if you didn't disable RDS Extended Support during the creation or restoration of your DB instances and DB clusters, then Amazon RDS will automatically enroll them in RDS Extended Support.

claim: Extended Support charges start the day after the RDS end of standard support date for every engine enrolled in Extended Support.
question: When do RDS Extended Support charges begin?

evidence.quote: You will incur charges for all engines enrolled in RDS Extended Support beginning the day after the RDS end of standard support date.

claim: RDS Extended Support charges also apply to standby instances in Multi-AZ deployments.

values.display: apply to standby instances in Multi-AZ deployments

claim: The Extended Support charge stops automatically when you upgrade to an engine version covered by standard support or delete the database that runs the old major version.

evidence.quote: The additional charge for RDS Extended Support automatically stops when you take one of the following actions:

claim: You can avoid Extended Support charges by changing the EngineLifecycleSupport parameter with the AWS CLI or RDS API; if the DB instance or cluster is already past its standard support end date, it then upgrades automatically to the next supported major version.
question: How do you opt out of RDS Extended Support, and what happens if the database is already past end of standard support?

values.display: automatically upgrades to the next supported major version

evidence.quote: You can also avoid being charged for RDS Extended Support by changing the enrollment status of an existing DB instance or DB cluster at any time by modifying the `EngineLifecycleSupport` parameter using the AWS CLI or the RDS API.

If you disable the enrollment status of a DB instance or DB cluster that is already past its standard support end date, the instance or cluster automatically upgrades to the next supported major version.

claim: Example from the guide: the RDS end of standard support for RDS for MySQL 5.7 was February 29, 2024; databases still on 5.7 were enrolled automatically in Extended Support that day, and charges started on March 1, 2024.

evidence.quote: In this case, Amazon RDS automatically enrolls your databases in RDS Extended Support on February 29, 2024, and you can continue to run RDS for MySQL version 5.7.

note: d26-010: 'charges from 2024-03-01' confirmed for MySQL 5.7; for PostgreSQL 11 the charges page gives April 1, 2024 as an example.
